Body & health 1

Name your body from head to toe in Thai. This topic teaches the parts themselves — the face, with ตา (eyes), หู (ears) and จมูก (nose); the bits that ache or get knocked, like เข่า (knee) and ข้อเท้า (ankle); and the parts under the skin — ปอด (lungs), สมอง (brain) and กระดูก (bone). It also covers the split Thai makes between ผม (head hair) and ขน (body hair). All 41 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations, and word-by-word notes, so the head-to-toe vocabulary settles by ear.

โรคกระเพาะ is an everyday catch-all for upper-stomach discomfort — closer to indigestion or an 'upset stomach' than a specific diagnosis. Thais widely blame it on eating at irregular hours, so this is a very common warning.
